summary: This was an open race because Republican Sen. John Cornyn was not the party's nominee. James Talarico (Democrat) defeated Ken Paxton (Republican).

candidates.name: James Talarico
candidates.bio: James Talarico has served in the Texas House of Representatives since 2018 and previously taught sixth-grade language arts in San Antonio. He is pursuing a Master of Divinity at Austin Presbyterian Theological Seminary.

positions.summary: Says he would raise taxes on billionaires and corporations and expand the Child Tax Credit and Earned Income Tax Credit.
Says he would let people of any age join Medicare as an alternative to private insurance, and would strengthen the Affordable Care Act.
Says he supports immigration reform that tightens border security, expands legal immigration and offers citizenship to long-term undocumented residents.
Opposes private school vouchers and says he led the fight against Gov. Abbott's voucher program in the Texas House.
Says he supports using all kinds of energy, protecting oil and gas jobs while expanding wind, solar and geothermal power.
Says he supports a federal law that writes Roe v. Wade into law, and to protect access to contraception and IVF.

candidates.name: Ken Paxton
candidates.bio: Ken Paxton has been Texas Attorney General since 2015 and previously served in the Texas House and Senate. He won the 2026 Republican Senate nomination in a May runoff after receiving President Trump's endorsement.

positions.summary: Sued to have the entire Affordable Care Act declared unconstitutional.
Says he will help President Trump deport people in the country illegally, secure the border and finish the border wall.
Says he will fight to cut taxes, stop wasteful federal spending, revitalize American manufacturing and make America the crypto capital of the world.
Says he will protect parental rights and oppose what he calls "woke indoctrination in our classrooms."
Says he will remove regulations that he says are designed to hurt energy companies.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35); also confirmed by fox4news.com report. Paxton beat Cornyn in May runoff; Talarico won in November (AP call).
